structure: Part 11 mined all 13 trace zips its read names, from six spec files in the tests repo's animals project, and read each spec in full: pages/transporter.spec.ts (4: renders the page controls [aca24]; lists both a commercial and a private transporter [1026d]; leaves every transporter unchecked on load [a1501]; accepts a transporter picked from the list [effbe]), pages/transporter-add.spec.ts (3: renders the page controls [0e072]; leaves the transporter type unchecked on load [eaf7d]; accepts a valid transporter type [640c4]), pages/transporter-selection.spec.ts (3: renders the page controls [b3f84]; leaves the transporter unchecked on load [1d694]; accepts a valid transporter [78ca8]), features/commercial-transporter-scope.spec.ts (1 [94ca6]), features/commercial-transporter-submission.spec.ts (1 [2bb3b]) and features/private-transporter-scope.spec.ts (1 [d4e42]). All 13 passed. The bundled trace viewer refuses these zips (TraceVersionError: recorded by a newer Playwright), so each zip was unzipped into this part's work folder and read with jq: N-trace.trace for the before/after actions and the frame-snapshot DOM rendered back to HTML, N-trace.network for the requests with their form bodies and redirect locations. Refs name the trace by its folder hash fragment and the call id. Every UI-driven test builds a fresh draft through the UI (origin, commodity, arrival details, one transit country) and reaches the transporter list from the transit countries page's Save and continue; the submission test seeds everything up to arrival details through the frontend's own form posts and resumes at transit countries. Pages in this slice, in the order a user meets them: (1) Transporter details, the transporter list at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/transporters (caption Transport and arrival; guidance paragraphs and bullets on transporter authorisation; a Search field and button; a Select a transporter table of small radios with Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status columns; Add a transporter; Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview). It always appears, reached from the overview task Transport details and after transit countries. Its rows mix commercial and private entries and also carry any transporter the trader hand-added, tagged New. (2) Choose a transporter type at /transporters/add (caption Add a new transporter), reached only by Add a transporter: a warning to search first, then Private transporter and Commercial radios. (3) Add commercial transporter at /transporters/add/commercial, shown only when the type is Commercial: a help notification banner, the authorisation number, name and address fields, a Country select fixed to Northern Ireland, and contact details. (4) Add private transporter at /transporters/add/private, shown only when the type is Private: name, address, a 32-country Country select and contact details. A partial fill shows a six-error summary. (5) Search for an approved commercial transporter at /transporters/select, reached here only by direct URL. It lists the 2 approved commercial transporters as radios with address and approval-number hints. (6) The overview's Transport details task status (To do or Complete) and (7) the end-to-end submission through the review page's Transport details summary card, the declaration and the Import notification submitted panel. What is conditional: the commercial page (type Commercial), the private page (type Private), the wipe of the other type's keyed-in record when the type changes, the checked state of a list row (the saved choice), and the New tag (hand-added rows). Network logs show only browser-to-frontend traffic, plus the address-book lookups the seeding helper makes. No backend or reference-data call is visible from the browser.
